Name: claims-auditor
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Checks a /ux-os:run work file: whether its claims table is complete and whether each citation supports its claim. Writes one audit file and edits nothing else.

Name: researcher
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: General research agent for interviews, usability tests, surveys, personas, journeys and synthesis, plus best-practice research. Consolidated from several role agents.

Name: init
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Connects a project's design system once. Deliverables take its fonts and colours, and each design proposal names a real component or says none fits. It shows you everything before saving.
Testing: Connected to one real design system with 133 components. The step that saves it has its own self-test, and running it twice changes nothing.

Name: record-decision
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Records what you decided because of the research, what the decision rests on and what would reverse it. A decision made on a belief stays in pencil.
Testing: The rules its file is checked against have their own self-test and one independent review. The typed command has not been run yet.

Name: research-debrief
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Takes in a new interview or study, removes the names, and shows which beliefs it bears on, without rewriting anything you built.
Testing: Run by an agent following the files, on made-up test data only.

Name: research-discover
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Asks what you believe about a new idea, once, then builds your first jobs, personas and journey from it and names the one belief to test first.
Testing: Run by an agent following the files, on made-up test data only.

Name: research-next
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Says where a research idea stands and the one thing to run next. It reads the folder and changes nothing.
Testing: Typed as a real command on a made-up idea, and it named the right next step. The routing has its own self-test.

Name: research-synthesize
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Once enough evidence is in, sorts it, summarises it, settles each belief and rebuilds your proto models on what people did.
Testing: Run by an agent following the files, on made-up test data only.

Name: run
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Runs someone else's design skill on an idea without changing it, then files the output with a table of every claim it rests on, each tagged. A separate auditor reads the table.
Testing: The briefing and the check have their own self-tests. Followed by agents on two walk-throughs. The typed command has not been run yet, and picks cover six interaction design jobs only.

Name: affinity-diagram
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Sorts real research notes into themes from the bottom up, counts people rather than notes, and has a second agent re-sort them blind. Needs data to work from.
Testing: Test run: 4 of 26 notes landed differently in the blind re-sort. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: analyze-card-sort
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Works out how people grouped your cards: how often pairs stayed together, the groups that form, and the cards with no clear home. Needs real results.
Testing: Analysis script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-diary-study
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A diary study people will finish: entries under two minutes, a plan for dropouts, and everything participants receive.
Testing: Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-empathy-map
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Maps what one person says, does, thinks and feels in one moment, and where saying and doing come apart. Works from your beliefs or from real research.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-interview-script
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A short guide built on real past events, with every question tied to something it tests, read cold by a second agent before anyone runs it.
Testing: Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-journey-map
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Maps what happens today, or what should happen in future, from your beliefs or from real research. A future journey is labelled as a proposal.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-jtbd
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Works out what people are trying to get done, apart from any product, from your beliefs or from the stories of people who actually switched.
Testing: A false belief planted in the test came back contradicted. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-personas
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Splits people on the behaviour that most changes what they need. Works from your beliefs, each one marked and tested, or from real research.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-research-repository
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: One place for what you've learned across studies, with each insight's strength and age, that answers questions without guessing.
Testing: Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-service-blueprint
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Lays out how a service delivers one scenario, step by step, with what the person sees above the line and what makes it work below.
Testing: The rules its file is checked against have their own self-test and one independent review. Filled once from an existing blueprint. The typed command has not been run yet.

Name: create-survey
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Writes the analysis first, then only the questions it needs, with sample sizes worked out by a script.
Testing: Sample size script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

Name: create-usability-plan
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Realistic tasks and pass lines set before anyone is tested, so the result can't be argued into a pass.
Testing: Run on made-up test data only.

Name: summarize-research
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Turns a transcript or a study into findings rated by how many people stand behind them, with what cuts against each. Needs real data.
Testing: Its draft passed the checks, but it hasn't yet written its output file in a test.

Name: design-research
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Personas, empathy maps, journey maps, interview scripts, surveys, diary studies, card sort analysis, usability test plans and synthesis. Switched back on 13 November 2026.

Name: lenny-skills research set
Author: RefoundAI
Summary: customer-interviews and analyzing-user-feedback, from a much larger skills library.

Name: design-system agent
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Drives live page violations to zero without changing how a page looks unless a person approves it.

Name: workshopr-uxdrift
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Audits a codebase for UX drift against its DESIGN.md and design-system JSON, and keeps the report to about fifteen findings so it gets read.

Name: Design System Enforcer
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Checks UI code against a design system's tokens and components.
Testing: Ships with its own test suite.

Name: adopt-ds
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Moves an existing page or app onto the system, replacing hardcoded colours and one-off styles.

Name: connect-ds
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Connects a repo that already has a design system, writing the profile the other ds-kit skills read.

Name: create-components
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Builds a first set of components from an inventory on shared conventions, with a machine-readable catalog and a real keyboard pass.
Testing: Final run, one case: 7 of 7 outcome checks with the skill, 6 of 7 without (12 of 12 with its own checks). 606s and $1.12 with, 40s and $0.14 without, the most expensive skill in the set. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: create-design-system
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Starts a design system from a live website, telling what a team meant from what drifted, and asks a person to rule on what the numbers cannot settle. Also takes a moodboard pick.
Testing: Final run, one case: 9 of 9 outcome checks with the skill, 8 of 9 without (20 of 20 with its own checks). 88s and $0.27 with, 38s and $0.17 without. A second case confirms it stops and asks when someone is there to answer. Trigger test 3 of 3.

Name: create-design-tokens
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Builds a tiered token layer in DTCG 2025.10, or rebuilds a flat pile in a live codebase without breaking what reads it.
Testing: Final run, one case: 8 of 9 outcome checks with the skill, 7 of 9 without (13 of 14 with its own checks). 151s and $0.37 with, 45s and $0.14 without. The one miss: a notice kept the same red in dark mode. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: create-ds-site
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Generates a documentation site from the system's own files so it cannot disagree with them, and fails when it goes stale.
Testing: Final run, one case: 6 of 6 outcome checks with the skill, 5 of 6 without (11 of 11 with its own checks). 283s and $0.19 with, 87s and $0.28 without. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: create-foundations
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Decides colour, type, space, grid, elevation and motion from the product's real conditions, with every number marked as observed, chosen, derived or assumed.
Testing: Final run, one case: 8 of 8 outcome checks with the skill, 5 of 8 without (13 of 13 with its own checks). 58s and $0.17 with, 84s and $0.22 without. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: create-icon-system
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Decides whether to adopt, curate or draw an icon set, then delivers a checked sprite, manifest and wrapper without quietly redrawing anything.
Testing: Final run, one case: 8 of 8 outcome checks with the skill, 8 of 8 without (15 of 15 with its own checks). 57s and $0.23 with, 53s and $0.16 without. No gain on outcomes alone; the gain is the contract and what it refuses to do. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: create-moodboard
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Chooses a visual direction before any tokens exist: two or three directions to pick between, written down as a brief.

Name: create-patterns
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Documents recurring compositions from real screens, and turns away what is only a page or a single component.
Testing: Final run, one case: 4 of 5 outcome checks with the skill, 1 of 5 without (10 of 11 with its own checks). 200s and $0.50 with, 42s and $0.18 without. The no-skill score swung from 5 of 5 to 1 of 5 between rounds, so read it as noisy. The one miss was a phrase the check did not recognise: the run did reject the hero. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: ds-governance
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Sets ownership and rules sized to the team, each rule either enforced by a gate or a named reviewer, or labelled a convention.
Testing: Final run, one case: 8 of 8 outcome checks with the skill, 4 of 8 without (13 of 13 with its own checks). 71s and $0.23 with, 33s and $0.11 without. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: migrate-ds
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Renames, deprecates, merges or removes a token or component, with a codemod rather than find and replace.

Name: release-ds
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Cuts a design-system version: decides the version number and writes the changelog.

Name: sync-ds-figma
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Pushes tokens to Figma variables and settles which side is right when Figma and code disagree.

Name: update-design-system
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: One change that spans tokens, components and names together, such as a rebrand or adding dark mode.

Name: update-ds-components
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Adds a component or changes an existing one's options, markup or API.

Name: update-ds-tokens
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Adds a design token or changes a value safely, including the one-line tweaks that look trivial.

Name: validate-ai-readability
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Measures whether a fresh AI agent can use a design system, by counting what it invents across blind builds.
Testing: Final run, one case: 7 of 7 outcome checks with the skill, 6 of 7 without (12 of 13 with its own checks). 110s and $0.71 with, 32s and $0.16 without. The one miss: that run did not render its builds, and said so. Trigger test 2 of 2.

Name: audit-ds
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Audits a design system against its own written rules. The project's checks run first, every finding quotes the line it was seen on, and what nobody read is said out loud.
Testing: Run once on a real design system with 97 components: 23 findings, each quoting its line, and seven contrast figures matched a separate recount. The gate caught no wrong fact there; a second reader caught them all, and the skill was revised because of it. Before that, two trial runs on a made-up system found every planted fault, and with no skill Claude quoted a lint result it had not run. The typed command has not been run.

Name: design-systems
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Tokens, component specs, naming, theming, icons, motion systems, governance, pattern libraries and accessibility audits.

Name: audit-system
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Audits an existing design system for consistency, completeness and accessibility.

Name: card-sort
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Plans open, closed and hybrid card sorts and analyses the results: similarity, clusters and cards with no clear home.
Testing: Analysis script with its own self-test.

Name: content-inventory
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Lists what a site or corpus holds and audits it: keep, revise, merge or retire. Samples large sets and says so.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test.

Name: content-models
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Content types, fields and relations for each template, and how the model constrains authors.
Testing: No script. Fired on its own request in the 9 Nov 2026 trigger check. Set result on the information-architecture row.

Name: create-object-map
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Works out the things a product is about before any page exists: the objects, how they relate and what people do with them.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example.

Name: create-sitemap
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Produces a sitemap as a file later stages build on: pages, hierarchy, template types and what is new or moving.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example.

Name: findability
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Works out why people can't find things, analyses search logs, and sets up synonyms, best bets and measures.
Testing: Search-log script with its own self-test.

Name: information-architecture
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: The front door for the set: scopes the job, holds the rules across it and routes to the eleven focused skills.
Testing: As one skill: 3 test cases, 3 rounds, every grade public. Latest round 28 of 29 with the skill, 19 of 29 without. Split into twelve: 28 of 29 in one run, against 25 for the single skill the same day.

Name: labeling
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Names for sections, menus and categories in the users' own words, checked with a predictability test.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test.

Name: navigation
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Menus, sidebars, footers, breadcrumbs and tab bars, with an entry rule for each surface and a plan for mobile and keyboard.
Testing: No script. Fired on its own request in the 9 Nov 2026 trigger check. Set result on the information-architecture row.

Name: redirect-maps
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Old-to-new URL maps for migrations and rebuilds, checked for chains, loops and coverage of every old URL.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test.

Name: site-architecture
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Plans or restructures a public website: which pages exist, where they live, their URLs, what goes in the header and footer, and how pages link so a visitor reaches a decision.
Testing: Blind test, three cases: 31 of 32 checks with this skill, 26 with the skill it replaced, 23 with no skill. Claude wrote the checks.

Name: sitemaps
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Decides the structure of a site, app or docs set: shape, depth, template types and one home for every item.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test.

Name: taxonomies
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Categories, tags, facets and controlled vocabularies, tested by applying them to the real content, with a governance loop.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test.

Name: tree-tests
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Plans tree tests and analyses the results: success with confidence intervals, directness and first clicks.
Testing: Analysis script with its own self-test.

Name: url-structure
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: URL rules and slug conventions a platform can enforce, and an audit of the URLs that exist.
Testing: Checking script with its own self-test.

Name: animation
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Whether something should move at all, then timing, easing, interruption and a reduced-motion version for each motion.
Testing: Script with 191 self-tests. Clean test, 9 Nov 2026: 11 of 11 with the skill, 11 of 11 with the old pack. Blind judge ranked it first. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone.

Name: conversational-interfaces
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Chatbots, AI assistants, agents and voice lines: what should be a conversation, how it repairs itself and what it may do.
Testing: Script with 122 self-tests. Hidden case by an independent author, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, old pack 10 of 10, no skill 10 of 10. Blind judge ranked it first. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone.

Name: error-handling
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: What a product does when things fail: who can fix it, what is at risk, what it says and what to fix first.
Testing: Script with 118 self-tests. Clean test, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, old pack 9 of 10, no skill 9 of 10. Blind judge ranked it last, before and after a length limit. Trigger check: chosen on 1 of 2, lost once to the old pack's error-flow; won with that pack off.

Name: feedback-states
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: What the interface says back after an action: control states, status, toasts, undo and confirmation.
Testing: Script with 103 self-tests. 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, old pack 10 of 10, but the writer saw the checks, so this shows only that it runs. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone.

Name: form-designs
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Which questions a form should ask at all, then labels, validation, autofill and errors, with an HTML audit script.
Testing: Script with 110 self-tests. Hidden case by an independent author, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, old pack 10 of 10, no skill 9 of 10; 10 of 10 after fixes. Blind judge ranked it last, before and after a length limit. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone.

Name: ios-interactions
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: iPhone gestures, sheets and haptics: what the system owns, conflicts, and a route for people who can't make the gesture.
Testing: Script with 124 self-tests. 9 Nov 2026: 11 of 11, old pack 11 of 11, but the writer saw the checks, so this shows only that it runs. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone. No VoiceOver or Switch Control run.

Name: laws-of-ux
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: All thirty laws from lawsofux.com: what each actually measured, where it stops holding and whether it applies here.
Testing: Script with 482 self-tests. Hidden case by an independent author, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, old pack 10 of 10, no skill 10 of 10; 10 of 10 after fixes. Blind judge ranked it last, before and after a length limit. Trigger check: chosen on 1 of 2, won with the old pack off.

Name: loading-states
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: What each screen does during a wait, worked out from measured timings: indicators, skeletons, optimistic updates and background jobs.
Testing: Script with 114 self-tests. Clean test, 9 Nov 2026: 11 of 11, old pack 10 of 11. Blind judge ranked it first. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone.

Name: micro-interactions
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A buildable spec for one small control: every state, input, failure and timing, with acceptance tests.
Testing: Script with 133 self-tests. 9 Nov 2026: 11 of 11, old pack 10 of 11, but the writer saw the checks, so this shows only that it runs. Trigger check: chosen on 0 of 2, losing both to the old pack; with that pack off, 1 of 2.

Name: search-design
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Query intent, suggestions, results, facets, AI answers and relevance testing with a scoring script.
Testing: Script with 75 self-tests. 9 Nov 2026: 11 of 11, old pack 10 of 11, but the writer saw the checks, so this shows only that it runs. Trigger check: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss went to findability as intended.

Name: user-onboarding
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: The first session by arrival path, activation, reading a funnel honestly and what traffic can detect, with a funnel script.
Testing: Script with 83 self-tests. 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, old pack 9 of 10, but the writer saw the checks, so this shows only that it runs. Trigger check outside the platform project: chosen on 2 of 2, near-miss left alone. Inside platform, a skillOverrides entry hides it from automatic selection.

Name: Emil Kowalski motion skills
Author: Emil Kowalski
Summary: animation-vocabulary, improve-animations, review-animations, emil-design-eng and apple-design.

Name: interaction-design
Author: MC Dean
Summary: States, forms, feedback, errors, loading, search, navigation patterns, micro-interactions and UX laws such as Fitts and Hick.

Name: animation-principles
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Applies animation principles, such as easing, staging and follow-through, to one specific motion.

Name: design-form
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Designs a form end to end: structure, decision points, chunking, validation, errors and completion.

Name: design-onboarding
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Designs a first-run experience: the activation path, progressive disclosure and time to first value.

Name: error-flow
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Designs an error flow end to end: prevention, detection, messaging and recovery.

Name: feedback-patterns
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Designs the confirmations, status updates and notifications that tell people an action registered.

Name: loading-states
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Designs the wait: spinners, skeletons, optimistic updates and progressive reveal.

Name: map-states
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Models a component's states and transitions end to end: states, events, guards and edge cases.

Name: designer
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: General UI and UX design agent covering wireframing, layout, information architecture and implementation-ready specs. Consolidated from five separate role agents.

Name: landing-page-design
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Copy strategy and look before any code, a hero-first build, gates against generic AI pages and a two-reviewer feedback round.
Testing: One dry run and two critic passes. The UX-OS landing page went through it too.

Name: Taste skills
Author: Leonxlnx
Summary: Frontend taste skills. This repo holds design-taste-frontend, and the high-end, minimalist and brutalist styles now live in taste-skill-classics.

Name: ui-design
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Colour, type scale, spacing, layout grid, responsive design, dark mode, visual hierarchy, platform conventions and the Gestalt laws.

Name: visual-critique
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Critiques hierarchy, colour, typography, composition, affordance, information density and brand consistency.

Name: impeccable
Author: Paul Bakaus
Summary: Designs, critiques, audits, polishes and animates frontends.

Name: create-content-strategy
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: What to publish, what to stop and who keeps the rest alive, sized to the team's real capacity.
Testing: Script with 105 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 10, old 10. Blind judge: new first, old second, no skill third. Round 1: no skill first, new last. Trigger check: 1 of 2.

Name: copy-editing
Author: Corey Haines
Summary: Edits and proofreads existing copy in a series of focused sweeps rather than one rewrite.

Name: humanizer
Author: blader
Summary: Finds and removes the signs of AI-written text, based on a public catalogue of those signs.

Name: ux-copy
Author: Anthropic
Summary: Writes or reviews UX copy: microcopy, error messages, empty states and calls to action. Part of the design plugin in the Claude desktop app.

Name: ux-writing
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Writes interface copy: microcopy, error messages, empty states and calls to action.

Name: create-annotated-wireframes
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Numbered annotations for handoff: what each element does, where its data comes from, its rules, states and accessibility.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example.

Name: create-interaction-flows
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Draws how a person gets a task done, including what happens when it goes wrong, before screens are designed.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example. One of three stages taken through the full eval loop.

Name: create-lofi-prototype
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A clickable low-fidelity prototype built from the wireframes, to test a flow before visual design.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example.

Name: create-screen-inventory
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Lists every screen a feature needs and what each must show, including its loading, empty, error and permission states.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example. One of three stages taken through the full eval loop.

Name: create-wireflow
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Lays wireframe thumbnails along a flow's arrows on one board, so a reviewer can walk the whole journey in a single view.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example.

Name: create-wireframes
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Greyscale wireframes of each screen, as files the next stages read, to review structure before visual design.
Testing: All eight Design OS stages pass a shared 96-rule checker on one worked example. One of three stages taken through the full eval loop. Plain Claude already scored 10 of 10 on the drawing checks, so the value here is the linking and checking.

Name: prototyping-testing
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Wireframe specs, user flows, parallel concepts, concept selection, prototype strategy, test scenarios, click tests, heuristic evaluation, accessibility test plans and A/B tests.

Name: prototype
Author: Matt Pocock
Summary: Builds a quick prototype to test an idea.

Name: user-flow-diagram
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Diagrams screen-level paths, decision points and branch logic for how a feature is traversed.

Name: align-stakeholders
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Works out what kind of disagreement it is, separates what was said from what is inferred, and gets a decision recorded.
Testing: Script with 124 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 10. Blind judge: new first, no skill second. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: analyze-competitors
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A competitive read that changes a decision, with every claim sourced and dated and a check on whether weights flip the ranking.
Testing: Script with 65 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: new first, no skill second. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: business-design
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Whether an idea can make money: the bet that would kill it, unit economics, pricing and the cheapest test.
Testing: Script with 79 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, no skill 9, old 8. Blind judge: new first, no skill second, old third. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: create-brief
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: One page that turns a request into an agreement about the problem, with contradictions and open questions first.
Testing: Script with 107 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, no skill 10. Blind judge: no skill first, new second, same as round 1. Trigger check: 1 of 2.

Name: create-design-principles
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Principles that settle arguments, ranked for when they collide and tested on disputes set aside first.
Testing: Script with 80 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: no skill first, new second. Round 1: new first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: create-experience-map
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Where an experience breaks across channels and owners, with every cell marked evidence or assumption.
Testing: Script with 92 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: no skill first, new second, same as round 1. Trigger check: 1 of 2.

Name: create-manifesto
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A manifesto of positions that cost something, each tested against a real decision, with receipts.
Testing: Script with 75 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: no skill first, new second, same as round 1. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: create-north-star
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A vision or a single metric, how it could be gamed, its guardrails and what a target really demands.
Testing: Script with 171 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: new first, no skill second. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: create-service-blueprint
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: What has to be true backstage for a promise to hold: lanes, owners, failures and recoveries, with times computed.
Testing: Script with 68 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 8 of 10, no skill 10, old 10. Blind judge: no skill first, old second, new third. Round 1: new first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

Name: design-strategy
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Design vision, strategy documents, org-level principles, investment cases and portfolio prioritisation.

Name: ux-strategy
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Problem framing, briefs, north star vision, opportunity frameworks, metrics, service blueprints, content strategy and its own information-architecture skill.

Name: ai-alignment-reasoning
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Guardrails, harm anticipation, trust calibration, transparency, consent and escalation.

Name: design-agent-orchestration
Author: MC Dean
Summary: How agents collaborate, hand off, recover from failure and stay legible to people.

Name: evaluation
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Behaviour evals, trust calibration and failure analysis for agentic experiences.

Name: model-interaction-design
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Conversation patterns, mixed-initiative flow, generative UI, context windows and frustration detection.

Name: prompt-architecture
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Structures prompts and context as a design material.

Name: system-behavior-shaping
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Defaults, guardrails, refusals and behavioural contracts.

Name: accessibility-decisions
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Documents and maintains accessibility decisions across teams and time.

Name: accessible-content
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Content that works for screen readers, cognitive differences and diverse literacy.

Name: adaptive-interfaces
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Design systems that respect user preferences and adapt to individual needs.

Name: cognitive-accessibility
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Cognitive load, plain language, wayfinding and focus.

Name: inclusive-interaction
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Multi-modal interactions that adapt to how people move, perceive and communicate.

Name: inclusive-personas
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Personas, user stories and scenarios that include disability from the start.

Name: UX program and leadership packs
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Eleven packs: program-planning, stakeholder-comms, delivery-execution, cross-functional-alignment, measurement-ops, process-design, people-management, team-building, org-influence, operating-cadence and leadership-craft.

Name: design-ops
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Handoff specs, critique and review process, design QA, sprints, design debt and impact reporting.

Name: designer-toolkit
Author: MC Dean
Summary: Design rationale, case studies, presentations, UX writing, negotiation and design-system adoption.

Name: Design Agent
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: A self-looping designer: critique, fix, re-render and re-score until an exit bar is met, then learn from the run.
Testing: An independent critic scores every pass.

Name: critique-partner
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Design critic that judges a page against the project's written rules. Every issue quotes a rule word for word and points at evidence on the page; anything no rule covers is labelled a judgment call.

Name: design-critic
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Independent scorer for each Design Agent pass. Looks at the rendered page and the code with fresh eyes, scores them against the contract and never fixes anything.

Name: feature-build
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Builds one slice of a planned feature and loops it until lint, tests, the design system and review all pass.
Testing: An independent reviewer scores every pass.

Name: feature-plan
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Interviews you into a spec, a design brief and build slices, then runs the feature pipeline.
Testing: Its test suites were all green on 20 Oct 2026.

Name: crit
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Interactive critique of a URL, page, screenshot or Figma frame against the project's own taste.md and design rules. It captures the page, asks what the page is for one question at a time, then runs the critique-partner agent.
Testing: A gate with 55 test cases, and two headless runs.

Name: create-project-files
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Sets up a project's nine UX-OS files (PRODUCT, DESIGN, AGENTS, PERSONAS, JOURNEYS, JTBD, taste, motion and VOICE) from annotated templates, writing only the ones that are missing.

Name: create-product-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's PRODUCT.md by interview, settling what the product is, who it is for and how you will know it is working.

Name: create-design-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's DESIGN.md by interview, settling the rules a check could enforce for how the product looks, reads and behaves.

Name: create-agents-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's AGENTS.md by interview, settling the pointer to the guide, the guardrails an agent must not miss and what "done" means.

Name: create-personas-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's PERSONAS.md by interview, as labelled beliefs about who the product is for.

Name: create-journeys-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's JOURNEYS.md by interview, as labelled beliefs about how each primary persona gets the job done today.

Name: create-jtbd-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's JTBD.md by interview, as labelled beliefs about the progress people are trying to make and what they hire for it today.

Name: create-taste-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's taste.md by interview, in the owner's own words, settling the judgment no check can enforce.

Name: create-motion-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's motion.md by interview, settling how motion feels, its values as tokens, the patterns allowed and what reduced motion does.

Name: create-voice-file
Author: Bill Bulman and Claude
Summary: Write or revise a project's VOICE.md by interview, settling how every word a user reads should sound, with examples from the product's own copy.
